sources.title: Official Mistral-Nemotron model card in Markdown
sources.evidence: HTML-linked Markdown card identifies a Mistral-produced, NVIDIA-optimized text model, v1, released on Build on June 11, 2025. It documents a modified Transformer, 128K context, translation, summarization and tools; its capabilities section explicitly enables reasoning and function calling. It gives no total or active parameter count. Local raw fetch succeeded even though the web renderer could not read this Markdown URL.

sources.title: Official endpoint page and embedded endpoint specification
sources.evidence: The indexed catalog names Mistral AI as provider and marks downloadable weights unavailable. Raw page endpoint metadata identifies mistralai/mistral-nemotron and explicitly sets modelCapability.functionCalling=true and reasoning=true; the playground enables reasoning by default. Its deprecation notice says API deprecated September 27, 2026 and unsupported after September 28. The embedded OpenAPI schema omits tools and reasoning controls and contains an MIT label linked to an inaccessible HF LICENSE; neither overrides the model card’s explicit licensing requirements. No endpoint inference was attempted.

sources.title: June 11, 2025 NVIDIA announcement
sources.evidence: The dated announcement explicitly calls Mistral Nemotron a new Mistral model, optimized jointly for inference and exclusively available through NVIDIA AI Enterprise. This independently supports the model card’s June 11 public release date.

sources.title: Mistral partner-served deployment terms
sources.evidence: Current terms, effective May 28, 2026, grant limited access/use of Mistral products through partners, retain Mistral ownership, and require confidentiality for weights made available through Specific Access. The exact card directs deployments to acquire Mistral licenses; proprietary is a descriptive classification, not a claim that these are public open-weight terms.

sources.title: License URL referenced by embedded endpoint OpenAPI
sources.evidence: HTTP 401 during direct retrieval; no license text obtained. The OpenAPI MIT label is not treated as proof of an MIT weight release.

sources.title: Mistral official-organization exact-name model search
sources.evidence: API returned an empty list for this exact model-name search; direct repository metadata also returned HTTP 401. This is corroboration of the catalog’s unavailable-download label, not proof that no private repository exists.

sources.title: NVIDIA official-organization exact-name model search
sources.evidence: API returned an empty list for this exact model-name search. Mistral-NeMo-Minitron repositories are differently named models and are not evidence for this endpoint’s counts.

sources.title: Current Mistral models and publication index
sources.evidence: Current public model cards and technical publication list do not identify this 2025 endpoint as another released checkpoint or disclose its parameter count. Exact-name searches across Mistral, NVIDIA research and arXiv did not locate an exact-model technical report. Counts for later Mistral models are not transferred.

sources.title: March 2026 Mistral-NVIDIA coalition announcement
sources.evidence: Describes a future co-developed base model underpinning Nemotron 4, separate from the already released June 2025 Mistral-Nemotron endpoint. It supplies no exact-model parameter count for this record.

sources.title: HTML model-card route and Markdown alternate link
sources.evidence: Direct HTML retrieval exposes only a shell plus an explicit alternate text/markdown link to s1. Full card content was obtained through that linked Markdown representation; missing HTML rendering is not represented as missing primary documentation.

name.note: Display punctuation normalized from the exact official Mistral-Nemotron name; wire identifier is mistralai/mistral-nemotron.

developer.note: The exact card explicitly says Mistral produced the model and that NVIDIA did not develop or own it. NVIDIA optimized inference and hosts the route. Correct the developer attribution; preserve the frozen catalog record ID.

family.note: Retains the catalog’s Nemotron name grouping, supported by this model’s official name; it does not imply NVIDIA authorship or the architecture of NVIDIA’s other Nemotron families.

release_date.note: Exact card declares this Build release date, independently corroborated by the same-day NVIDIA announcement of the new model. June 12 is the page update date, not the release.

open_weights.note: Official catalog marks downloads unavailable and the card requires acquiring licenses from Mistral for deployment/customization. No public exact-model checkpoint was found; private licensed weight access is distinct from open weights.

license.note: Exact card requires NVIDIA trial terms for the hosted API and a Mistral license for deployment. Embedded API-schema MIT metadata points to an inaccessible file and is not substantiated as a model-weight license. Use the descriptive proprietary classification.

parameters_b.note: No total count is disclosed in the full exact card or endpoint documentation. Exact-name primary-report searches and official repository searches found no count-bearing checkpoint/report. A third-party 70B claim has no located primary support and is not adopted; do not substitute NeMo, Minitron, Llama Nemotron or later coalition models.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-per-token count is disclosed for the exact endpoint. No public checkpoint or routing configuration was available to derive one; neither total nor dense structure is assumed.

architecture.note: Exact card explicitly specifies Transformer / Modified Transformer. It does not disclose whether layers are dense or sparse MoE, nor block dimensions; transformer is the supported classification.

context_window.note: The card specifies a 128K maximum context for input/output. Retains the catalog’s decimal normalization to 128000; source does not establish a precise 131072-token configuration or a separate output allowance.

modalities.note: The exact card explicitly specifies text-string input and output.

reasoning.note: Current exact-model capabilities explicitly mark reasoning supported and endpoint playground metadata enables reasoning by default. This supports true without inferring from math benchmarks; no controllable reasoning budget or API toggle is claimed.

tool_call.note: The exact card describes tool calling and its capability metadata explicitly enables function calling. Embedded OpenAPI schema does not expose tools fields, so record documented model capability without claiming a tested currently operational tool endpoint.

description.value: Mistral AI text model optimized by NVIDIA for instruction following, coding, translation, summarization and tool use.
description.note: Plain description follows the exact model card and official endpoint description, with correct developer and optimization roles.

patch.description: Mistral AI text model optimized by NVIDIA for instruction following, coding, translation, summarization and tool use.
patch.notes: Mistral AI developed this model; NVIDIA optimized and hosted it. The official card describes a modified Transformer with 128K context but does not disclose total or active parameters or dense/MoE structure. Public weights are unavailable; deployment requires a Mistral license. The embedded API schema’s MIT label is not backed by an accessible license. Current capability metadata marks reasoning and function calling supported, but NVIDIA’s page also says this API was deprecated September 27, 2026 and unsupported after September 28; current endpoint operation was not tested. The catalog ID retains its original provider-based prefix.

Official endpoint page and embedded endpoint specification

summary: Corrected developer to Mistral AI, architecture to documented modified Transformer, proprietary licensing and reasoning support; retained primary-confirmed June 11, 2025 release, 128K context, text modalities and tool capability. Total and active counts remain undisclosed after exact-model primary searches. Notes distinguish deprecated endpoint documentation from current service operation and reject an unsupported embedded MIT label. Parent integration aligns the derived developer_id to mistral while preserving the frozen model ID.
